title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Hints on the right argument, counts the panel agrees with
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.26 fixes what the counters and the hints showed: a parameter hint placed inside a string, "0 usages" on every symbol of the default package, a lens count that disagreed with the panel it opened, a Test Explorer that skipped `src/testDebug/` and reported a `@DisplayName` test as skipped, and test names with spaces that Gradle on Windows never found.

highlights.title: Hints land on the argument
highlights.description: A comma inside a string, a comment among the arguments or a raw string spanning lines no longer shifts the parameter hints, and an imported library function stops wearing a workspace homonym's parameter names.

highlights.title: One count, lens and panel
highlights.description: Only the declaration token is left out of the count, a cancelled lens request no longer leaves a partial count behind, and symbols in the default package finally have usages.

highlights.title: Tests found and matched
highlights.description: Every Gradle test source set is discovered, a @DisplayName test gets its result, @Nested classes run on every Gradle version, and test names with spaces survive cmd.exe.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Parameter hints skip commas and brackets inside strings, raw strings and comments, and a call inside a multi-line block comment gets none.
A `launch(a, b)` call under `import kotlinx.coroutines.launch` no longer shows the parameters of the project's own `launch`.
The lens and the panel exclude the same declaration token, a cancelled request never caches a partial scan, and two files without a `package` line reference each other.
Raw-string text is not a usage (its `$name` templates are), and a `/*` opened mid-line hides the following lines until `*/`.
The Test Explorer discovers `src/testDebug/` and `src/screenshotTest/`, matches `@DisplayName` tests, targets `@Nested` classes under both spellings, and quotes test names on Windows.
